landing.title: Get feedback that real players never give you.
landing.lead: A gated circle of game developers who test each other's games. Play a build, record your session, answer the dev's questions — earn Credits. Spend Credits to get your own game tested by people who know what to look for.

tutorial.title: How Playtest Circle works
tutorial.lead: Two minutes to read. Submitting your own game takes about 5 minutes.
tutorial.step1Body: Open Browse, pick a game that looks interesting, read what the dev wants to know, then press Start playtest. The game opens in a new tab and you share that tab, so the whole page is recorded — UI included. Play, mark interesting moments, answer the questions. When you reach the minimum playtime and answer every required question, the Credits are yours automatically.
tutorial.step2Body: In My studio, add your game: title, a one-line pitch, the link where it can be played (itch.io, Wavedash, your own site…), a cover, screenshots, a trailer and an optional short hover clip.
tutorial.step3Body: Pick the questions you need answered from the best-practice catalog (or write up to 5 of your own), choose how long testers should play, how many tests you want and how many Credits you pay for each. Higher pay = faster tests. Credits are held in escrow and only paid for completed tests.
tutorial.step4Body: Every session lands in your campaign: watch the recording, jump to marked moments, read ratings and comments, and give the tester a thumbs up or down. Recordings are deleted after 3 days — delete them sooner once you've watched them and get 1 Credit back.
tutorial.tip1: You start with {n} Credits — enough for your first small campaign, but the circle runs on testing first.
tutorial.tip2: Recording works in desktop Chrome, Edge and Opera.
tutorial.tip3: You can quit a test early — just tell the dev why. Credits are only paid once the minimum playtime is reached.
tutorial.tip4: Email on every finished playtest is on by default. Change it in Settings.

steam.step1Body: This is a Steam game: open its Steam page, install it and start it (see the access notes for keys or playtest access). Come back here once for step 2.
steam.step2Body: In the dialog, choose "Window" and select the game's window (or "Entire screen" if it runs fullscreen). Recording starts the moment you share — then switch to the game and play.

controls_feel.hint: Weight, precision, input delay, whether moves do what you expect.

controls_responsive.text: How responsive is the game to your input?
controls_responsive.hint: Any lag, dropped inputs or animations you have to wait for?

controls_intuitive.text: I knew how to control the game without reading anything.
controls_intuitive.hint: Note every moment you had to guess a key or button.

onboarding_goal_clear.text: Within the first minute I understood what I'm supposed to do.
onboarding_goal_clear.hint: When exactly did the goal click — or did it never?

onboarding_first3.text: How well do the first 3 minutes hook you?
onboarding_first3.hint: Would you keep playing if you'd found this game on a portal?

onboarding_tutorial.hint: Too long, too short, too wordy, skipped something important?

progression_short.text: Does progression work in the first minutes?
progression_short.hint: Do you feel yourself getting stronger or better quickly enough?

progression_long.text: Does the progression system look like it works long-term?
progression_long.hint: Is there a reason to come back tomorrow? What would you grind for?

progression_rewards.hint: Name a reward that felt great and one that felt pointless.

difficulty_curve.text: How well does the difficulty ramp up?

difficulty_missing_challenge.text: There were stretches where a challenge was missing.
difficulty_missing_challenge.hint: Where did you play on autopilot?

difficulty_unfair.text: Some moments felt unfair rather than hard.
difficulty_unfair.hint: Deaths you couldn't see coming or couldn't avoid.

bosses_too_hard.text: A boss was too hard to be fun.
bosses_too_hard.hint: Which boss, how many attempts, what killed you?

bosses_too_easy.text: A boss was so easy it gave no reason to keep playing.
bosses_too_easy.hint: Did any boss fall before you learned its pattern?

bosses_readable.text: How readable are the boss attacks?
bosses_readable.hint: Telegraphs, warning signs, time to react.

pacing_boring.text: Where would you drop out because it gets boring?
pacing_boring.hint: Give the moment or the timestamp — mark it while you play.

pacing_one_more.text: I had the "one more try" feeling.
pacing_one_more.hint: What gave it to you — or what was missing?

stuck_where.text: Where did you get stuck, and for how long?
stuck_where.hint: Being lost, not knowing what to do next, a puzzle that didn't click.

stuck_confusing.hint: Which one, and what did you think it did?

ui_readable.text: How readable is the UI and text?
ui_readable.hint: Font size, contrast, clutter, important info you missed.

ui_feedback.text: How clear is the game's feedback on your actions?
ui_feedback.hint: Hits, damage, rewards, errors — did you always know what happened?

audio_quality.hint: Music fit, volume balance, annoying loops.

audio_feedback.text: Sound effects help me understand what's happening.
audio_feedback.hint: Hits, warnings, pickups — would you miss them if muted?

visuals_style.text: How appealing is the visual style?
visuals_style.hint: Would it make you click on a thumbnail?

visuals_clarity.text: How clear is the screen during action?
visuals_clarity.hint: Can you tell player, enemies, hazards and pickups apart?

performance_smooth.text: How smoothly does the game run?
performance_smooth.hint: Frame drops, stutters, long loading. Mention your device.

performance_bugs.hint: What you did, what happened, what you expected. Mark the moment.

overall_fun.text: How much fun did you have?
overall_fun.hint: Be honest — that's what the circle is for.

overall_return.text: I'd play this again after the playtest.

sys_overall.text: Overall, how ready does this build feel?
sys_overall.hint: Your gut feeling as a fellow dev.

sys_stuck.text: Anything else the dev should know?
sys_stuck.hint: Bugs, ideas, the one change you'd make first.

sys_quit_reason.text: Did you stop before the target playtime? Why?
sys_quit_reason.hint: Required if you stopped before the minimum.

privacy.s1Body: When you sign in with Google we store your Google account ID, name, email address and profile picture. We also store what you do on the platform: your games, campaigns, playtests, answers, marked moments, ratings and your Credit history. We never get your Google password.
privacy.s2Body: During a playtest, only the browser tab you choose to share is recorded — picture and sound, plus your microphone if you turn it on. A recording can only be watched by the developer of the game you tested and by you. Recordings are deleted automatically after 3 days at the latest. If storage runs low, recordings are deleted earlier: first the ones the developer has already watched (oldest first), then the oldest remaining ones.
privacy.s3Body: We use exactly one cookie: your session cookie, which keeps you signed in. It is strictly necessary and is not used for tracking. Your colour scheme and Browse layout are remembered in your browser's local storage. There is no analytics, no advertising and no tracking.
privacy.s4Body: Google (sign-in), Cloudflare (hosting, database), Backblaze B2 (storage of recordings and game media) and Gmail (notification emails, only if email notifications are on). If you add a Discord webhook, notifications are also sent to Discord.
privacy.s5Body: You can see your data on the platform at any time, turn email notifications off in Settings and delete your account there. Deleting your account removes your personal data and every recording you are part of. Under the GDPR you also have the right to information, correction, restriction and objection — contact us via the imprint.
privacy.s6Body: The entire source code of Playtest Circle is public on GitHub, so you can check exactly what happens with your data.

terms.s1Body: Playtest Circle is a free community for game developers. One account per person. Be respectful: you're testing a colleague's work.
terms.s2Body: Play the game seriously and answer the questions honestly. Credits are paid automatically once the minimum playtime is reached and all required questions are answered. Abuse of the system (fake sessions, idle recordings, multiple accounts) leads to a ban.
terms.s3Body: Only games you have the rights to. No malware, no phishing, no illegal content. Mature content must be clearly stated in the pitch. We may hide campaigns that break these rules.
terms.s4Body: Credits are a community currency for playtests. They currently have no monetary value and cannot be exchanged for money. Buying Credits and payouts are planned for the future and will come with their own terms.
terms.s5Body: As a developer you may watch recordings of your own playtests for improving your game. Don't publish or share them without the tester's permission.
